name: Supabase
verdict: Self-serve: add an OAuth app in organization settings, with no review documented, likely in 1-3 days. Scopes are fixed at creation, so changing them forces users to re-authorize.
needGuide: Short one, but pick scopes carefully because changing them forces re-authorization.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow for the Management API: authorize at https://api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/authorize (client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state, optional organization_slug), exchange at POST https://api.supabase.com/v1/oauth/token with Basic auth. PKCE (S256) is strongly recommended. Refresh tokens work via the same endpoint; access-token lifetime is not stated. Revoked access makes refresh fail with 401.

approval.gate: No review documented. The guide says the OAuth app must be 'published' before use, without explaining how; likely just saving it in org settings. Scopes are fixed at app creation; changing them forces users to re-authorize.

scopes.why: Per-app Read/Write scopes set at creation; no scope triggers approval.
scopes.summary: Per-app scopes set at creation: Auth, Database, Domains, Edge Functions, Environment, Projects, Rest, Secrets (Read/Write), Organizations and Storage (Read only). The authorize 'scope' parameter is deprecated. Only some features are available until fine-grained access control rolls out. No scope triggers approval.

cost: Free (requires a Supabase organization; plan requirements not stated)
prerequisites: Account and owner: Create the app inside an organization your company owns, in the org settings. Which org roles can create apps is not documented; use an Owner (likely safest).
Where you register: Dashboard → Organization settings → OAuth Apps → Add application → fill details → Confirm
Cost: Free (requires a Supabase organization; plan requirements not stated)

registerAt.path: Dashboard → Organization settings → OAuth Apps → Add application → fill details → Confirm

steps.do: Open Dashboard → Organization settings → OAuth Apps in a company-owned org
Add application: name, website, redirect URI(s), select scopes (Auth, Database, Domains, Edge Functions, Environment, Projects, Rest, Secrets, read-only Organizations/Storage); Confirm
Save client ID and secret in a secrets manager
Redirect users to /v1/oauth/authorize with state and PKCE S256 code_challenge; validate state on callback
POST /v1/oauth/token with Basic auth, code, redirect_uri and code_verifier; store refresh token encrypted; handle 401 by refreshing or re-authorizing
Test end to end against a scratch project and a second account; verify re-authorize after scope change

roles.team: Create the app inside an organization your company owns, in the org settings. Which org roles can create apps is not documented; use an Owner (likely safest).
roles.customer: The authorizing user selects which of their organizations to grant. Their org role limits what the token can do (likely Owner/Admin for project management). Token access is described as full Management API access, restricted only by app scopes.

testing: Create the app in your own org and authorize with your own account; no sandbox.
Use a throwaway Supabase project for create/delete tests.

blockers.problem: Database password cannot be fetched via the Management API
blockers.fix: Collect it from the user in your UI for existing projects.

blockers.problem: Changing scopes later forces every user to re-authorize
redirect_uri plus state must not exceed 4 kB

blockers.fix: Confirm in the dashboard or with Supabase support before launch.

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth/PKCE client, token refresh logic and Management API calls, and draft the app description and scope justification.
automation.humanMust: Log in to the dashboard and create the OAuth app; a customer user must consent and choose an organization.

uncertain: Access-token lifetime, which org roles can create apps, what 'publish' entails, and rate limits were not documented in fetched pages.
Community sources not consulted; fetch limit reached before further checks.
